claims.text: TypeSafe announces System One Models with Jev in early access: a new model architecture with parallel sampler and RLCD training, emitting typed probabilistic outputs instead of generated strings.
claims.context: Launch page fully consumed this pass (published 2026-09-15, founder Diogo Almeida, ex-OpenAI/ChatGPT research).

claims.text: The launch claims ~70-500ms end-to-end (40-200x faster), $0.042/MTok input with free outputs, no-type-error guarantees by construction, and Pareto-frontier workflow evals vs GPT-6 Astra/Fable 5.1 average as reference (193.6x faster / 444.6x cheaper at the high end).
claims.context: Vendor-evaluated; page's own nuance sections disclose laptop-based evals, workflow-authorship bias, and reference-answer bias toward OpenAI/Anthropic.

claims.text: The launch discloses evaluation limits directly: speed/cost measured from West-Coast laptops, workflows built by its own capabilities team, LLM baselines run through its System One adapter wrapper, hallucination numbers for LLMs sourced from OpenRouter routing.
claims.context: First-party nuance admissions; material to the Jev limitations case.

limitations.text: Independent reproduction of latency/price/accuracy claims outstanding (D073 community leads only).
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

limitations.text: RLCD algorithm internals not disclosed on this page; architecture detail limited to sampler/output semantics.
